description:
MEASURED s492c (Opus, 2026-09-21) while checking #1997's warm-cost gate.

`lib/POSIX.pm` grew from 98 to ~430 source lines (1,748 emitted CL lines), and
the first measurement looked alarming:

    ./runpcl 'use POSIX; print 1'   base 0.93 s  ->  tree 2.44 s   (+1.5 s)
    ./runpcl 'print 1'              base 0.18 s  ->  tree 0.19 s

The whole +1.5 s is SBCL compiling the shim, and the cause is the RUNNER:
`runpcl` spawns SBCL with `--eval "(setf pcl::*pcl-skip-cache* t)"`, so the
module-fasl cache (#1202/#1841's machinery) is switched off and every shim is
recompiled per run.  Through `./pcl`, which is what a user runs:

    ./pcl -e 'use POSIX; print 1'   base 0.047 s -> tree 0.052 s   (+5 ms)
    ./pcl -e 'print 1'              base 0.040 s -> tree 0.039 s
    PCL_FASL_DEBUG=1 says "module POSIX.pm -> FASL HIT (0.006s)".

So there is no user-visible regression, and the shipped shim is under
#1997's 0.1 s gate.  What is worth deciding is whether the DEV runner should
keep paying it: every `Pl/t` row that goes through a runner with the cache off
pays the compile of every shim its program loads, and that is most of the
gate's wall time for module-heavy rows.  A first attempt at making PCL's own
shim lib/ a compile-cached class (like `:extension`, task #1202's argument --
"it is PCL's own tree, not a directory the user edits") was written and
REVERTED as unnecessary: shims already reach the fasl cache when the cache is
on at all.  The question is only about the runner's switch.
subject: PERF (dev runners): ./runpcl sets *pcl-skip-cache*, so EVERY lib/ shim is transpiled and SBCL-compiled again on every run -- `use POSIX` is 2.4 s under runpcl and 0.05 s under ./pcl
